cells.remarks: Issued from Vañjulavāka. Records the grant, made by the king, of the field called Valivukhaṇḍa together with its gṛikā-bhūga, etc., in Sīlādīvī grāma in the Ramalavā vishaya situated in the Khinjalī-maṇḍala, for his merit and for the merit of his parents. The donee was the Brāhmiṇa named Bhaṭṭa Purushōttama who belonged to Krishnā- trēya-gōtra, Chhandōga-charana and Kauthuma sakhā and who was the son of Bhaṭṭa Aṅgaddika, grandson of Bhaṭṭa Vōka and great-grandson of Bhaṭṭa Gōvardhana. (with the consent of the other authorities viz., Aniyasta (two officers) of Śrī-Jayamahābhiśēki, who are described as Vāygārika and Mantrin respectively; conveyed by Mahā- pratīhāra Kumada; written by the Sāndhivigrahi Jaya- tambha; and engraved by the Akshasālin Dulē’gadēva. Published in JBORS, Vol. VI, pp. 276 ff.; cf. Bhandarkar's List, No. 1502; cf. no. S above and no. 44 below.

cells.remarks: Appears to record the royal ratification of the grant of Vōṇali- grāma made tax-free, situated in the Uttara-khāṇḍa in the Sidhādi-vishaya, made by the king samyagākimēja Narāṇ- drabhañja, the son of Prithvibhañja for the merit of his parents and himself for obtaining the grace of god Bhagavān Mahādēvabhaṭāraka. Published in JBORS, IV, pp. 175 ff., and Plate; cf. Bhandarkar's List, No. 1488.

Ibid., Vol. VIII, pp. 138 ff., and Plate.

cells.remarks: Late. Damaged. Records the grant by purchase made by the king, of the village Svētavāṭikā at the request of the Mahāsāmanta Mahārāja Achyuta to the Mahāyānikabhikshu- sangha constituted for ever or the āryya-bhikshu (Avalōkitēś- padraka-mahāvihāra presided over by āryya-sthavira [Avalōkitēś- vara] for worship and offerings and for the feeding etc. of the Arya-samgha therein. It appears that the above vil- lage was entrusted to the same Mahāsāmanta Achyuta with the provision that he should pay annually the Samghika- Ārūpadaka-dhānyaka(cōna?) probably the Saṅghikā- Ārūpadaka-dhānyaka (coins?). It appears that the king participated in the transaction. The plate was heated by the Pushpāpala Bhōgabhaṭṭa and was engraved by Kayastha Mānadatta. It is engraved by Chhānas. In characters of about the 6th century A. D. Published in OHRJ, Vol. XI, pp. 206, ff., and Plate.

cells.remarks: Commences with a eulogy in Sanskrit of the chief, Mēḍa Timma-nāyuḍu, son of Chennama-nāyuḍu and records the construction of a śilāmaṇṭapa with prākāra and gōpura, tanks and wells and the laying out of some gardens for the Chennakēśava temple. cells.remarks: Records that Appaya and Gōpaya, the sons-in-law of Sāluva Timmarasu and sons of Nādināḍla Timmarāju, having renovated, at their own cost, the caumfi named Dēvukūṭam leading to Timmasamudram named after Timmarasa created a now village called Lakshmīmāpuram in the name of their mother Lakshmīmāmbā, wife of Timmarasu and granted the same on the occasion of dēvākāryam for the merit of Sarajadiamma for the merit of their grand-parents Also records an endowment of 3 tūmu of wet-land in the newly created village to Ayalōjhala Yara Timmayya for conducting the worship and abhiśhēka and nityanandadāna every Monday to the deity. cells.place: Pillar in the Śiva temple on the bank of the tank locally called "Gulavā Ṭilā".
cells.remarks: Records the installation of the five deities Arka, Gaṇapa, Śivā, Śrīśa and Gaurīśa in one temple and Bhairava and Hanumān in another temple. cells.location: Raipur
cells.place: M.G. Museum. Stone slab ('broken into two'), originally in the Nagpur Museum, Nagpur. Findspot: Raipur [tahsil(?), Chaṇḍā 'District, Mahārāshtra.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Records the restoration of a Buddhist vihāra by two persons, one of them, a learned Brāhmaṇa (name lost) who had studied the teachings of Sugata (i.e., the Buddha) and was a favourite of Bhavadēva, and the other, a Buddhist Brahmachārin named Nambuddha, authorized to bear the title of āchārya at the instance of Bhavadeva. The vihāra is stated to have been originally founded by a king named Sūryaghōsha. The composer of the prasasti, 1905, pp. 617 ff., and Plate. Also see Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII, pp. 251-50.

cells.location: Sāgar
cells.place: Slab kept in the Museum attached to the Department of Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology in the University. Findspot: Sōṅkapā, Raipur District.
cells.date: Vikrama 1312, Bhādrapada śu. 7, Monday=1256 A.D., August 28.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a temple to god Śambhu and the grant of some land for its maintenance in Guḍāśarkaraka-grāma by Durgadatta, son of Vīradatta, who was a resident of Śrīpura. The construction of the temple to a Śaiva ascetic named Sadāśivāchārya, the praishya of the brother of Sadāśiv-āchārya, who hailed from the penance-grove of called Amardaka. Also records a gift of some land in Kōṭṭavī-grāma and Vīyaka-grāma and the Śrīparṇikā-grāma in Lāṭa to the same ascetic with the stipulation that a sacrifice should be performed on the full-moon day of the months of Āshāḍha, Kārttika and Māgha every year, that the faithful should be engaged in the worship of the deity, etc. It is established. The record was composed by Sunanagala, son of Tārādatta and engraved by Vāsuṇaga, son of Rīshigaṇa. In characters of the 7th century A. D. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, p. 31 ff., and Plate.

cells.place: Same wall, right of entrance
cells.date: Year 15, Rishabha, śu. 11, Thursday, [Svāti]=1268 A.D., May 24.
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines built in. The images were set up by Akaḷaṅka-nāḷvār in the name of Nāyakar Viśaiyālayadēvar, and used as utsava images. Dēvan of Tirumeni-aḷagiyār of Koḍumbāḷūr, the accountant of Vadaṭūr, figures as the signatory of the record.

cells.remarks: Records the arrangement made for the contribution of oil-seeds from the villages of Vaṇpūḍu at stipulated rates for burning 300 lamps daily in the temple of Tiruvāḷavāram-uḍaiya-Tambirān by the nāṭṭār of Vaṇpūḍu in Kār-kāttūr-nāḍu. cells.place: Slab in the Mahādeva temple. Impression received from Shri D. R. Amladi, Department of Archaeology, Maharashtra, Aurangabad.
cells.remarks: In verse. Incomplete and damaged. Mentions Jejākabhukti in the introductory verse. Contains a genealogical account of the Yādava dynasty upto the death of Simhana. cells.remarks: Records that out of 100 nivartanas of land which Devěda- Yogīśvara had obtained from Vāsugi-seṣṣi for worship and charity, 12 nivartanas to the deity Yogīśvara to the south- east of Mārīī-nagara, his son Govinda-Yogīśvara made a grant of 50 nivartanas to the deity Yogīśvara, installer in the agrahāra of Davādīge in Hagariīge-300, retaining the remaining 50 nivartanas for the deity Yogīśvara of Gavāra- vara. Also records that a house in the village of Hiriya-Uluhe was granted to the two deities (i.e., Gavā-rěśvara-Yogīśvara and Davādīge-Yogīśvara). Ibid.

cells.date: Year 4, Pramādi, Śrāvaṇa śu. 12, Monday, Uttarāyāṇa-day, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records that Karuva Guigmayya, a subordinate of Iriva-beḍagandēva caused to be built a pūjāmaṇḍapa, a stone temple, a satra, a śālā, a manne and a village gate. Guigmayya and his brother Barmayya, a temple architect, were entrusted into the hands of the 400 mahājanos of Alavani for their maintenance. The record was written by Malli. Guigmayya is further stated to have made many other gifts including feeding of ascetics and footwears to brāhmaṇas, nānādēsi and others. Also refers to the death of Guigmayya after having led the life of a recluse. Published in Sāsana-parichaya, No. 20.

cells.date: Śaka 1125, Dundu-bhi, Māgha ba. Amāvāsye, Monday, solar eclipse. Irre-gular.
cells.remarks: Contains a long eulogy of the 400 mahājanas of Aḷavaṇḍi and records a grant of houses and land, with their permission to god Ranganātha of Chāḷukya-Vikrama-pura, the capital of the mahājanas, described as vijaya-śrī-mānyam. Also records two grants of lands, totalling 12 mattar to the same deity by Gaṅgarasa. Further records that Saṅkaṇa, the mahāpradhāna of Biḷḷayya, the son of the king and the queen Kētalādēvi, granted a house-site and some land, and the income from hejjunka and other taxes to the same deity. Refers to the Ubhaya-nānādēśis, Mummuri-daṇḍas and the 500 svāmis of Ayyāvaḷe. Noticed in Sāsana-pari-chaya, No. 21.

cells.location: SOUTH KANARA DISTRICT / MANGALORE TALUK / Kadiri — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab fixed on the floor in the kitchen of the Mañjunātha temple.
cells.remarks: Beginning effaced. Refers to the samastapradhānas, dēśipurushas and the sāmanta-bhaṭṭarāniyarāga as present when the king was seated in the audience. In characters of the 12th century. Cf. No. 376 of SII, Vol. VII.

cells.location: Chittorgarh
cells.place: Slab lying in the office of the Western Sub-Circle, Archaeological Survey of India. Impressions received from the Superintendent, Archaeological Survey of India, Western Circle, Baroda.
cells.remarks: Partly damaged and fragmentary. Records that a Brāhmaṇa named Nṛsiṁha, the son of Bālājā and grandson of Someśvara, belonging to Vatsa gotra and Prāgvāṭa-jñāti and Jñāntīya-gaḍha, constructed a Śiva temple named after Baliśā, and a lake said to have resembled the Jambhūkhārī-saras built by Māyā, and planted a grove near it. Mentions his brother of Narasimha. The praśasti was composed by Vēdāchārya. The engraver was Karmasiṁha. See Bhandarkar's List, Nos. 583 and 610.

cells.remarks: Contains four verses in praise of three Jaina teachers, viz., Guru Jinabhakti-sūri who died at Maṁgādvīpara; his pupil Pāvakēndra who died in the town of Rājagaṁha in Sāṅgalī-durgga; and his pupil Sāhasaprabha who died at Śrī-vara-Jaisala-gadha. Mentions the Jaina Jinaharaṣṇa-sūri belonging to Bṛhat-Kharatara-gachchha and refers to the pādukā (foot-prints) of the three above-mention-ed gurus in the dharmasālā.

cells.location: Siyākārā
cells.place: Pedestal of the image in the Jain temple.
cells.date: Vikrama 1961, Śāka 1826, Māgha śu. 11, Wed- nesday=1905 A.D., February 15.
cells.remarks: Records the installation of an image of Mālavinātha Pārśva- nātha in Siyākārā-grāma by Kamalasēna-sūri of the Tapā- gachchha, the disciple of Hēmavimala-sūri of the Tapā- gachchha, on the occasion of the kṛtotsava of the Upakēśa- jñāti in Sāṇā-grāma. The record was written by Muṁ° (Munī?) Padmasāgara and Gū (Gaṇī) Puṇyasāgara. Also records that an image of Śāntinātha, an image of Pārśvanātha by Lambā and Māmingā, sons of Sāchavī, residents of Sāṇāpura village; of an image of Nēminātha by Vīrachandra, etc., sons of Mūlachandra; and of a kṛtotsava on the śikhara of the main shrine by Bhālā and Jēssā, residents of Sādara (Sīdar) village.

cells.location: DEWAS DISTRICT Iṭāgōḍā
cells.place: Stone-slab built into the wall of a newly built temple.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king. Records the grant of the village Aḍḍāyaka to god Gōhādēvaradēva whose temple was situated in the southern part of the village Iṭāgō-padra by the king for his and his parents' spiritual merit. The writer was Kaihaṇa, son of Rājēśvara belonging to a Kāyastha family of Vālabh-anvaya and the engraver was Sājana, the son of Harasēṇa who was the son of Sūtradhāra Mahābala of Kukāś(?)-anvaya. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. VI, pp. 55 ff., and Plate. Cf. Bhāṇḍārkar's List, No. 229 and p. 391. Also see IHQ, Vol. XXXV, p. 9.

cells.location: Māndhātā
cells.place: Slab built into the wall near the Nandi in front of the Oṁkāra temple.
cells.date: Vikrama 1704 (vēda-mōna-bāṇa-indu), Āṣāḍha ba. uk-dhyā (i.e., 15?), Tuesday, corresponding to the solar eclipse = 1647 A.D., June 22. (The year was Chaitrādi and the month was Pūrṇimānta.)
cells.remarks: In two sections. In the first section the genealogy of the king is given. The second section in bolder characters records the visit of the king to Māndhātā and to the temple of Oṁkarēśvara where he performed the ceremony of the (i.e., tulā-purusha) with gold and silver on the occasion of the solar eclipse. The composer of the praśasti was Mukunda, son of Sūtradhāra Bhānu. Mentions Pachōlī Araṇyajita and Sūtradhāra Mukundabhānu and Gajadhara.

cells.location: Bījāpur
cells.place: Slabs in the Archaeological Museum in the Naubat Khāna, Gol-Gumbad. Slab No. 1.
cells.remarks: Records the text of an order issued to the nā'ib-i-ghibat (king's deputy), dān(o)dār and kārkuns of the mu‘āmala of Bījāpur, stating in response to a request made to the Nawwāb (i. e. the king) Muḥammad ‘Alī Ḥajjām, to exempt the poor barber community from the payment of Kalmīra, Barīd and other imposts (ghair-qānūn), which were levied on the Ḥajjām (barber) community of the said town, in the interest of the welfare of the people of the city of Bidar and Khurāsān (i. e. Irān). His August Majesty the Nawwāb was pleased to remit these imposts and also exempts the barbers from garrison duties. In characters of 10th-11th centuries A. H. Published, M. Nāzim, Memoire of the Archaeological Survey of India (MAS), No. 49, p. 85, no. 3247, pl. X.

Also records that Malik Ghāzī made a legal endowment of a garden and the shops that he had built in or near the Athinbīl gate, for the mosque, which was situated in front of his house, so that the expenses for the maintenance of its building, water-storage, public water-place, etc., could be met from the income of the house and the shops. cells.location: Jāmi‘-Masjid †
cells.place: Dargāh of Chīngīz-Pīr. On a pillar. Do.
cells.remarks: Badly damaged. Records the text of a gaulnāma issued by the chief among ministers and nobles, recipient of the much coveted epithet son' (farzand) from the king, Afẓal Khān Muhammad Shāhī, conqueror of the country of Malnād, and subject to the order of the king and at the request of Muhammad, an official, in respect of a paif (town, name not specified) founded by him. The gaulnāma states that if any of the merchants, jewellers, Chātis, grocers, high and low, expired without leaving any heir, their property, both movable and immovable, including jewels, male and female slaves, etc., should not be confiscated to the State, but should be distributed among his relatives in the presence of the Qāḍī and other grandees and leading men of the town, to be used for the benefit of the poor, the orphans and the needy. Written by Ḥājī Sayyid Isḥāq Ḥaqqānī, son of 'Alī-al-Khānī, scribe. Ibid., pp. 82-83, No. 3318. Also see No. 290 above and No. 328 below.

cells.remarks: States that the object of setting up this stone is to announce that the step-well (bāolī) outside the postern gate (‘arīz-i-darwāza) of the road to Shāhpur, outside the postern gate (‘arīz-i-darwāza) of the capital city of Bijāpur, was built in his own life-time by the late Malyā, son of Nāg Sottī, a resident of the city, and he has provided it for the use of the ownership of the step-well which provides water to the people of the city, settled with him (and his descendants) and to no one else. Ends with an imprecation against those who seek to interfere in the said property right. Cf. ibid., pp. 65-66, No. 497.
